text:
Ava (Head of Product): thanks all — following up from today's all-hands on pricing/packaging. drop short questions here and we'll answer. (we'll consolidate into an FAQ afterward)

Mike (Billing PM): does usage of embeddings count against the same "credits" pool as text generation? curious for customers doing hybrid workloads.

Ava (Head of Product): short answer: yes, they draw from the same credits balance by default, but we surface per-product breakdowns in billing. you can configure separate quotas for embeddings vs generation on Dedicated/Private.

Jess (Eng Lead): on the Dedicated side, are rate limits applied per-tenant or per-GPU-pool? trying to explain to a customer.

Riley (SRE): per-tenant policy by default. for capacity-based throttling we also enforce pool-level admission to protect latency SLOs. think: tenant quota -> pool admission -> per-connection limits.

Sam (Customer Success): what happens when a customer hits their credits cap? immediate cutoff or soft degrade?

Mike (Billing PM): primary behavior is soft cap first: we notify + degrade non-critical requests (background batches, low-priority routes). then hard cap if overage protection is off. customers on committed plans can opt-in for auto-topup or emergency burst.

Ava (Head of Product): addtl: we rolled out "graceburst" policy for certain long-term customers — small emergency buffer for one-off incidents. not automatic for all accounts.

Sam (Customer Success): can we get a short one-pager to give customers: "What to expect when you hit quota"? I can attach in onboarding.

Ava (Head of Product): yes — will publish a short FAQ. @Mike can you draft and I'll review?

Mike (Billing PM): on it. target: publish by EOW.

Jess (Eng Lead): question re: rate-limits vs quotas: if a request gets rate-limited (429), does it still consume token credits?

Riley (SRE): 429s don't consume token credits. if the request was accepted and we generated text then it counts. will add a note in the docs.

Sam (Customer Success): a customer asked if credits roll over monthly. what is current policy?

Mike (Billing PM): credits generally expire after the monthly period unless you have a committed/enterprise contract with rollover enabled. promo/dev credits have their own expiry windows.

Ava (Head of Product): for clarity: we differentiate three credit buckets in the UI: dev promo credits, monthly usage credits, committed/reserved credits. rollover only applies to committed buckets if the contract specifies it.

Jess (Eng Lead): small technical ask — can we get an example config for separate quotas for embeddings vs generation in Private? gave a customer a YAML example in the thread earlier but they want an official snippet.

Ava (Head of Product): good call. @Jess can you drop an example and @deploy-bot can pin it to the docs channel?

Jess (Eng Lead): pasted snippet:```yaml
quotas:
  embeddings:
    monthly_units: 500000
  generation:
    monthly_tokens: 20000000
```
(very simple sample)

Mike (Billing PM): also clarifying: overage billing only applies to generation tokens right now; embeddings overages convert to the equivalent credits unit at the end of the billing period unless blocked.

Sam (Customer Success): one customer requested a temporary raise for a launch window next month — what's the fastest path?

Mike (Billing PM): fastest is self-serve increase in Console (if on hosted), or contact Customer Success for Dedicated/Private and we can provision a temp bump w/ a short contract amendment.

Ava (Head of Product): action items: 1) Mike to draft "hit quota" one-pager, 2) Jess to add Private YAML examples, 3) Riley to add 429/credit docs note. we'll collect and publish as a single FAQ.

Riley (SRE): noted — I'll add the 429 bit to the rate-limit doc and link it in the FAQ.

Sam (Customer Success): thanks — I'll flag customers who asked and share when the FAQ is live. :thumbsup:

Ava (Head of Product): thanks everyone. if you have follow-ups DM me or drop here. closing thread in ~24h and moving to docs repo. :white_check_mark:
